title: Australia’s foreign-investment gatekeeper needs defence expertise | The Strategist
paragraphs: A common misunderstanding is that governments need public support for big national security decisions. If a government waits for public backing, it will act only when the populace demands a response to a crisis – and that, by definition, will be too late. European reaction to Russian aggression has been a prime example. Governments knew they should be bolstering defences, even as voters didn’t.

So let’s not make the same mistake with the Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) and wait for it to make some damaging national-security mistake, one that causes public outrage, before we reform it.

Its composition needs attention now. Amid global wars and conflicts and our own region’s tensions, the importance of Australia’s defence industrial base is hardly in doubt. To protect it from ill-judged decisions on foreign investment, the government should appoint a board member with substantial practical experience in defence capability development, acquisition, sustainment and industrial mobilisation.
